title: Extensibility & Foreign Code — Where It Stands
thesis: The most honestly-mixed group in the survey. Softanza consumes a large, carefully-vendored foreign-code stack (tree-sitter, SQLite, curl, mbedTLS, zlib, ggml, RmlUi, HarfBuzz, PCRE2, all compiled from source) and bridges pragmatically to Python/R/Julia/C/Prolog/Node by subprocess, but the extensibility the group is named for is overwhelmingly planned: no in-process FFI, no embedded interpreter, and the plugin plane ('a plugin is governed foreign capability') is a detailed plan with a recovered reference archive but zero live code.

lanes.note: A vendored C/C++ stack compiled from source via Zig (tree-sitter, SQLite, curl, mbedTLS, zlib, ggml, RmlUi, HarfBuzz, PCRE2); no external runtime deps
stz_polyglot parses Python and JavaScript (vendored grammars, no interpreter) into a declaration/call protocol feeding stzCodeGraph; two grammars, parse-only
Subprocess bridges stzDotCode (Graphviz dot), stzQmlCode (Qt qml runtime), stzImgToAscii (vendored im2ansi.exe); stzImgToAscii ships but is never loaded
stzExterCode runs Python, R, Julia, C, Prolog and Node via temp file + stzSystemCall + eval(); subprocess-only, hardcoded d: paths, suite currently red
Haro shims to paste Python, PHP, C#, Perl, C ternaries and SQL-in-Haro over stzTable; shims not a runtime, the JS shim is an empty stub, suite red
Both interop suites have real assertions but are entirely red: C22 function-redefinition, 0 passing (echo/range0 defined in both PHP and Python shims)
None for user code: no dlopen / cffi / direct-C-call surface; the only call-out is the subprocess bridge, an order of magnitude heavier
None: no in-process Python / JS / Lua interpreter embedded in the engine; foreign execution is subprocess-only
A plan of record (PL0-PL5) and a recovered/ archive marked reference-only; state_* VM primitives exist; no live code, not loaded, no test dir
Designed five-clause contract: isolation, per-call ledger, cooperative constraint, currency, governance; XfU reversal and @plugin_author provenance; unbuilt
Designed two-tier isolation (:State state / :Process reactor spawn); explicitly refuses to be a syscall-level security sandbox; unbuilt
None, and the plugin plan explicitly states it is not a package manager, marketplace or code-signing scheme; deliberately deferred

standouts: Strong foreign-code integration: a dozen serious native libraries built from source with no runtime dependencies
Governed foreign capability (designed): accept code you don't trust, audit what it did, undo it
The recovered 2024 plugin system proves per-call VM-state isolation works (~3.1 ms/call)
gaps: Fix the red interop suites (C22 duplicate shim definitions, 0 passing)
Configurable toolchain discovery (retire the hardcoded d: interpreter paths)
